title: Sell Mineral Rights in Vilonia, AR
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Vilonia, AR | Faulkner County
metaDescription: Own minerals near Vilonia, AR? Faulkner County was drilled hard during the Fayetteville Shale boom. Get a cash offer priced off your actual production.
heroLead: Faulkner County was one of the four core counties of the Fayetteville Shale, and Vilonia's stretch of it saw dense horizontal drilling from the mid-2000s on.
intro: Vilonia sits inside a county that operators leaned on hard during the Fayetteville Shale build-out, with SEECO and XTO both running horizontal programs through the Faulkner County core alongside their work further north in Cleburne and Van Buren. If your family owns minerals on land near Vilonia, there's a decent chance it's pooled into a unit that's been producing for close to two decades now, which puts most of these wells well into their long, low-volume decline tail rather than early in their life.

sections.heading: Faulkner County's Core Position
paragraphs: Vilonia falls inside the historical core of the Fayetteville play, so drilling density around town tends to be higher than in flank counties to the east. That usually means a tract here is pooled with multiple wells rather than a single one, which matters for how we price the interest.

sections.heading: Ownership Patterns We See Around Vilonia
paragraphs: A lot of the minerals in this area trace back to farm and pasture land that predates the 2000s boom, so it's common for an interest to have passed to two or three heirs without the division order ever being formally updated. We check the Faulkner County Circuit Clerk's records before quoting a number, so the offer reflects who actually owns what today.

faqs.question: My royalty checks from land near Vilonia have gotten small. Is the well done?
faqs.answer: Probably not done, just deep into its decline curve. Fayetteville Shale wells drop steeply in year one and then settle into a long, low-volume tail, which is where most Faulkner County wells are today.

faqs.question: Do you buy fractional interests split among several heirs?
faqs.answer: Yes, we buy individual heirs' shares directly and can work around the rest of the family holding onto theirs, as long as your specific percentage is documented.

faqs.question: How is my Vilonia tract priced?
faqs.answer: Off trailing royalty income, the well's remaining decline, and recent comparable trades in the same pooled unit, not a flat per-acre figure.

faqs.question: What records do you need to make an offer?
faqs.answer: A recent royalty statement or division order is the fastest start. If you don't have one, we can pull the lease and pooling order from the Faulkner County Circuit Clerk ourselves.

faqs.question: How long does it usually take to close on a Vilonia-area mineral interest?
faqs.answer: A single-owner tract with clean title can close in a matter of weeks. If the interest passed through several heirs without an updated division order, we build in extra time to confirm the probate history before finalizing anything.
